FORMAT_VERSION.D: This value is incremented when changes are made to the eeprom format

PILOT_THR_FILT.D: Throttle filter cutoff (Hz) - active whenever altitude control is inactive - 0 to disable

PILOT_THR_BHV.D: Bitmask containing various throttle stick options. TX with sprung throttle can set PILOT_THR_BHV to "1" so motor feedback when landed starts from mid-stick instead of bottom of stick.

GCS_PID_MASK.D: bitmask of PIDs to send MAVLink PID_TUNING messages for

RTL_CONE_SLOPE.D: Defines a cone above home which determines maximum climb

RTL_LOIT_TIME.D: Time (in milliseconds) to loiter above home before beginning final descent

RTL_ALT_TYPE.D: RTL altitude type. Set to 1 for Terrain following during RTL and then set WP_RFND_USE=1 to use rangefinder or WP_RFND_USE=0 to use Terrain database

FS_GCS_ENABLE.D: Controls whether failsafe will be invoked (and what action to take) when connection with Ground station is lost for at least 5 seconds. See FS_OPTIONS param for additional actions, or for cases allowing Mission continuat

GPS_HDOP_GOOD.D: GPS Hdop value at or below this value represent a good position. Used for pre-arm checks

SUPER_SIMPLE.D: Bitmask to enable Super Simple mode for some flight modes. Setting this to Disabled(0) will disable Super Simple Mode. The bitmask is for flight mode switch positions

WP_YAW_BEHAVIOR.D: Determines how the autopilot controls the yaw during missions and RTL

FS_THR_ENABLE.D: The throttle failsafe allows you to configure a software failsafe activated by a setting on the throttle input channel

FS_THR_VALUE.D: The PWM level in microseconds on channel 3 below which throttle failsafe triggers

THR_DZ.D: The deadzone above and below mid throttle in PWM microseconds. Used in AltHold, Loiter, PosHold flight modes

FLTMODE1.D: Flight mode when pwm of Flightmode channel(FLTMODE_CH) is <= 1230

FLTMODE2.D: Flight mode when pwm of Flightmode channel(FLTMODE_CH) is >1230, <= 1360

FLTMODE3.D: Flight mode when pwm of Flightmode channel(FLTMODE_CH) is >1360, <= 1490

FLTMODE4.D: Flight mode when pwm of Flightmode channel(FLTMODE_CH) is >1490, <= 1620

FLTMODE5.D: Flight mode when pwm of Flightmode channel(FLTMODE_CH) is >1620, <= 1749

FLTMODE6.D: Flight mode when pwm of Flightmode channel(FLTMODE_CH) is >=1750

FLTMODE_CH.D: RC Channel to use for flight mode control

INITIAL_MODE.D: This selects the mode to start in on boot. This is useful for when you want to start in AUTO mode on boot without a receiver.

SIMPLE.D: Bitmask which holds which flight modes use simple heading mode (eg bit 0 = 1 means Flight Mode 0 uses simple mode). The bitmask is for flightmode switch positions.

LOG_BITMASK.D: Bitmap of what on-board log types to enable. This value is made up of the sum of each of the log types you want to be saved. It is usually best just to enable all basiclog types by setting this to 65535. Note that if you

ESC_CALIBRATION.D: Controls whether ArduCopter will enter ESC calibration on the next restart. Do not adjust this parameter manually.

TUNE.D: Selects parameter (normally a PID gain) that is being tuned with an RC transmitter's knob. The RC input channel used is assigned by setting RCx_OPTION to 219.

FRAME_TYPE.D: Controls motor mixing for multicopters. Not used for Tri or Traditional Helicopters.

DISARM_DELAY.D: Delay before automatic disarm in seconds after landing touchdown detection. A value of zero disables auto disarm. If Emergency Motor stop active, delay time is half this value.

PHLD_BRK_RATE.D: PosHold flight mode's rotation rate during braking in deg/sec

LAND_REPOSITION.D: Enables user input during LAND mode, the landing phase of RTL, and auto mode landings.

FS_EKF_ACTION.D: Controls the action that will be taken when an EKF failsafe is invoked

FS_EKF_THRESH.D: Allows setting the maximum acceptable compass, velocity, position and height variances. Used in arming check and EKF failsafe.

FS_CRASH_CHECK.D: This enables automatic crash checking. When enabled the motors will disarm if a crash is detected.

RC_SPEED.D: This is the speed in Hertz that your ESCs will receive updates

ACRO_BAL_ROLL.D: rate at which roll angle returns to level in acro and sport mode. A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster. For helicopter sets the decay rate of the virtual flybar in the roll axis. A higher value cau

ACRO_BAL_PITCH.D: rate at which pitch angle returns to level in acro and sport mode. A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster. For helicopter sets the decay rate of the virtual flybar in the pitch axis. A higher value c

ACRO_TRAINER.D: Type of trainer used in acro mode

THROW_MOT_START.d: Start motors before throwing is detected
THROW_MOT_START.D: Used by Throw mode. Controls whether motors will run at the speed set by MOT_SPIN_MIN or will be stopped when armed and waiting for the throw.

THROW_ALT_MIN.D: Minimum altitude above which Throw mode will detect a throw or a drop - 0 to disable the check

THROW_ALT_MAX.D: Maximum altitude under which Throw mode will detect a throw or a drop - 0 to disable the check

THROW_ALT_DCSND.d: Throw mode target altitude to descend
THROW_ALT_DCSND.D: Target altitude to descend during a drop, (must be positive). This allows for rapidly clearing surrounding obstacles.

THROW_ALT_ACSND.d: Throw mode target altitude to ascsend
THROW_ALT_ACSND.D: Target altitude to ascend during a throw upwards (must be positive). This allows for rapidly clearing surrounding obstacles.

WP_NAVALT_MIN.D: Altitude in meters above which navigation will begin during auto takeoff

THROW_NEXTMODE.D: Vehicle will switch to this mode after the throw is successfully completed. Default is to stay in throw mode (18)

THROW_TYPE.D: Used by Throw mode. Specifies whether Copter is thrown upward or dropped.

DEV_OPTIONS.D: Bitmask of developer options. The meanings of the bit fields in this parameter may vary at any time. Developers should check the source code for current meaning

FRAME_CLASS.D: Controls major frame class for multicopter component

TUNE_MIN.D: Transmitter Tuning minum value. The parameter being tuned will have its value set to this minimum value when the tuning knob is at its lowest position

TUNE_MAX.D: Transmitter Tuning maximum value. The parameter being tuned will have its value set to this maximum value when the tuning knob is at its highest position

FS_VIBE_ENABLE.D: This enables the vibration failsafe which will use modified altitude estimation and control during high vibrations

FS_OPTIONS.D: Bitmask of additional options for battery, radio, & GCS failsafes. 0 disables all options.
v: bit0: Continue if in Auto on RC failsafe
bit1: Continue if in Auto on GCS failsafe
bit2: Continue if in Guided on RC failsafe
bit3: Continue if landing on any failsafe
bit4: Continue if in pilot controlled modes on GCS failsafe

ACRO_OPTIONS.D: A range of options that can be applied to change acro mode behaviour. Air-mode enables ATC_THR_MIX_MAN at all times (air-mode has no effect on helicopters). Rate Loop Only disables the use of angle stabilization and uses

AUTO_OPTIONS.D: A range of options that can be applied to change auto mode behaviour. Allow Arming allows the copter to be armed in Auto. Allow Takeoff Without Raising Throttle allows takeoff without the pilot having to raise the thrott
v: bit1: Allow Takeoff Without Raising Throttle

GUID_OPTIONS.D: Options that can be applied to change guided mode behaviour
v: bit3: SetAttitudeTarget interprets Thrust As Thrust
bit6: Waypoint navigation used for position targets

FS_GCS_TIMEOUT.D: Timeout before triggering the GCS failsafe

RTL_OPTIONS.D: Options that can be applied to change RTL mode behaviour

v: bit2: Release gripper on thrust loss

RNGFND_FILT.D: Rangefinder filter to smooth distance. Set to zero to disable filtering

GUID_TIMEOUT.D: Guided mode timeout after which vehicle will stop or return to level if no updates are received from caller. Only applicable during any combination of velocity, acceleration, angle control, and/or angular rate control

SURFTRAK_MODE.D: set which surface to track in surface tracking

FS_DR_ENABLE.D: Failsafe action taken immediately as deadreckoning starts. Deadreckoning starts when EKF loses position and velocity source and relies only on wind estimates

FS_DR_TIMEOUT.D: DeadReckoning is available for this many seconds after losing position and/or velocity source. After this timeout elapses the EKF failsafe will trigger in modes requiring a position estimate

ACRO_RP_RATE.D: Acro mode maximum roll and pitch rate. Higher values mean faster rate of rotation

ACRO_RP_EXPO.D: Acro roll/pitch Expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

ACRO_RP_RATE_TC.d: Acro roll/pitch rate control input time constant
ACRO_RP_RATE_TC.D: Acro roll and pitch rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

ACRO_Y_RATE.D: Acro mode maximum yaw rate. Higher value means faster rate of rotation

ACRO_Y_EXPO.D: Acro yaw expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

ACRO_Y_RATE_TC.d: Acro yaw rate control input time constant
ACRO_Y_RATE_TC.D: Acro yaw rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

PILOT_Y_RATE.D: Pilot controlled yaw rate max. Used in all pilot controlled modes except Acro

PILOT_Y_EXPO.D: Pilot controlled yaw expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

PILOT_Y_RATE_TC.d: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant
PILOT_Y_RATE_TC.D: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

TKOFF_SLEW_TIME.d: Slew time of throttle during take-off
TKOFF_SLEW_TIME.D: Time to slew the throttle from minimum to maximum while checking for a successful takeoff.

TKOFF_RPM_MIN.D: Takeoff is not permitted until motors report at least this RPM. Set to zero to disable check

PLDP_THRESH.D: Ratio of vertical thrust during decent below which payload touchdown will trigger.

PLDP_RNG_MAX.d: Payload Place maximum range finder altitude
PLDP_RNG_MAX.D: Maximum range finder altitude in m to trigger payload touchdown, set to zero to disable.

PLDP_DELAY.D: Delay after release, in seconds, before aircraft starts to climb back to starting altitude.

PLDP_SPEED_DN.D: The maximum vertical decent velocity in m/s. If 0 LAND_SPD_MS value is used.

SURFTRAK_TC.D: Time to achieve 63.2% of the surface altitude measurement change. If 0 filtering is disabled

TKOFF_THR_MAX.d: Takeoff maximum throttle during take-off ramp up
TKOFF_THR_MAX.D: Takeoff maximum throttle allowed before controllers assume the aircraft is airborne during the takeoff process.

TKOFF_RPM_MAX.D: Takeoff is not permitted until motors report no more than this RPM. Set to zero to disable check

FS_EKF_FILT.D: EKF Failsafe filter cutoff frequency. EKF variances are filtered using this value to avoid spurious failsafes from transient high variances. A higher value means the failsafe is more likely to trigger.

TUNE2_MIN.D: Minimum value that the parameter currently being tuned with the transmitter's TRANSMITTER_TUNING2 knob will be set to

TUNE2_MAX.D: Maximum value that the parameter currently being tuned with the transmitter's TRANSMITTER2_TUNING knob will be set to

TUNE2.D: Selects parameter (normally a PID gain) that is being tuned with an RC transmitter's knob. The RC input channel used is assigned by setting RCx_OPTION to 220.

PILOT_ACC_Z.D: The vertical acceleration used when pilot is controlling the altitude

PILOT_SPD_UP.D: The maximum vertical ascending velocity the pilot may request in m/s

PILOT_SPD_DN.D: The maximum vertical descending velocity the pilot may request in m/s. If 0 PILOT_SPD_UP value is used.

PILOT_TKO_ALT_M.D: Altitude that altitude control modes will climb to when a takeoff is triggered with the throttle stick.

SURFTRAK_GLSAM.D: When this many consecutive samples are considered a glitch, we give up and accept the new reading. A value of zero disables this behaviour and glitched values are never accepted.

FLTMODE_GCSBLOCK.D: Bitmask of flight modes to disable for GCS selection. Mode can still be accessed via RC or failsafe.

ADSB_LIST_RADIUS.D: ADSB vehicle list radius filter. Vehicles detected outside this radius will be completely ignored. They will not show up in the SRx_ADSB stream to the GCS and will not be considered in any avoidance calculations. A value

ADSB_LEN_WIDTH.D: Aircraft length and width dimension options in Length and Width in meters. In most cases, use a value of 1 for smallest size.

ADSB_OFFSET_LAT.D: GPS antenna lateral offset. This describes the physical location offset from center of the GPS antenna on the aircraft.

ADSB_OFFSET_LON.D: GPS antenna longitudinal offset. This is usually set to 1, Applied By Sensor

AFS_ENABLE.D: This enables the advanced failsafe system. If this is set to zero (disable) then all the other AFS options have no effect

AFS_MAN_PIN.D: This sets a digital output pin to set high when in manual mode. See the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

AFS_WP_COMMS.D: Waypoint number to navigate to on comms loss

AFS_WP_GPS_LOSS.D: Waypoint number to navigate to on GPS lock loss

AFS_TERMINATE.D: Can be set in flight to force termination of the heartbeat signal

AFS_TERM_PIN.D: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

AFS_AMSL_ERR_GPS.d: Error margin for GPS based AMSL limit

AFS_QNH_PRESSURE.D: This sets the QNH pressure in millibars to be used for pressure altitude in the altitude limit. A value of zero disables the altitude limit.

AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS.d: Maximum number of GPS loss events
AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS.D: Maximum number of GPS loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on GPS recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of GPS loss events.

AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS.d: Maximum number of comms loss events
AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS.D: Maximum number of comms loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on comms recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of comms loss events.

AFS_GEOFENCE.D: This enables the geofence part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

AFS_RC.D: This enables the RC part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY.d: Enable RC Termination only in manual control modes
AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY.D: If this parameter is set to 1, then an RC loss will only cause the plane to terminate in manual control modes. If it is 0, then the plane will terminate in any flight mode.

AFS_DUAL_LOSS.d: Enable dual loss terminate due to failure of both GCS and GPS simultaneously
AFS_DUAL_LOSS.D: This enables the dual loss termination part of the AFS system. If this parameter is 1 and both GPS and the ground control station fail simultaneously, this will be considered a "dual loss" and cause termination.

AFS_RC_FAIL_TIME.D: This is the time in seconds in manual mode that failsafe termination will activate if RC input is lost. For the OBC rules this should be (1.5). Use 0 to disable.

AFS_MAX_RANGE.D: This is the maximum range of the vehicle in kilometers from first arming. If the vehicle goes beyond this range then the TERM_ACTION is performed. A value of zero disables this feature.

AFS_OPTIONS.D: See description for each bitmask bit description

AFS_GCS_TIMEOUT.D: The time (in seconds) of persistent data link loss before GCS failsafe occurs.

AHRS_GPS_USE.D: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Cu

AHRS_RP_P.D: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude

AHRS_TRIM_Y.D: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.

AHRS_EKF_TYPE.d: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation
AHRS_EKF_TYPE.D: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation

AHRS_OPTIONS.D: This controls optional AHRS behaviour. Setting DisableDCMFallbackFW will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in fly-forward flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DisableDCMFa

AHRS_ORIGIN_LAT.D: AHRS last origin latitude in degrees

AHRS_ORIGIN_LON.D: AHRS last origin longitude in degrees

AHRS_ORIGIN_ALT.D: AHRS last origin altitude in meters

AIS_LIST_MAX.D: AIS list size of nearest vessels. Longer lists take longer to refresh with lower SRx_ADSB values.

AIS_TIME_OUT.D: if no updates are received in this time a vessel will be removed from the list

AROT_HS_P.D: Increase value to increase sensitivity of head speed controller during autonomous autorotation.

AROT_FWD_SP_TARG.D: Target ground speed in cm/s for the autorotation controller to try and achieve/ maintain during the glide phase.

ATC_LAND_Y_MULT.D: Yaw gain multiplier active when landed. A factor of 1.0 means no reduction in gain while landed. Reduce this factor to reduce ground oscitation in the yaw axis.

ATC_ANGLE_MAX.D: Maximum lean angle in all flight modes

ATC_RATE_WPY_MAX.D: Maximum rate the yaw target can be updated in Auto, Guided, Circle, Follow, RTL, SmartRTL, Throw and ZigZag flight modes

AVD_F_ACTION.D: Specifies aircraft behaviour when a collision is imminent

AVD_W_ACTION.D: Specifies aircraft behaviour when a collision may occur

AVD_F_RCVRY.d: Recovery behaviour after a fail event
AVD_F_RCVRY.D: Determines what the aircraft will do after a fail event is resolved

AVD_OBS_MAX.d: Maximum number of obstacles to track

AVD_W_DIST_Z.D: Closest allowed projected distance before BEHAVIOUR_W is undertaken

AVD_F_DIST_Z.D: Closest allowed projected distance before BEHAVIOUR_F is undertaken

CHUTE_TYPE.D: Parachute release mechanism type (relay number in versions prior to 4.5, or servo). Values 0-3 all are relay. Relay number used for release is set by RELAYx_FUNCTION in 4.5 or later.

CHUTE_ALT_MIN.D: Parachute min altitude above home. Parachute will not be released below this altitude. 0 to disable alt check.

CHUTE_CRT_SINK.d: Critical sink speed rate in m/s to trigger emergency parachute

v: bit0: hold open forever after release
bit1: skip disarm before parachute release

v: bit0: RC pitch and roll control radius and rate
bit2: Start at center rather than on perimeter
bit3: Make Mount ROI the center of the circle

INS_HNTC2_FREQ.D: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This is the center frequency for static notches, the center frequency for Throttle based notches at the reference thrust value, and the minimum limit of center frequency

INS_HNTC2_BW.D: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz. This is typically set to half the base frequency. The ratio of base frequency to bandwidth determines the notch quality factor and is fixed across harmonics.

INS_HNTC2_ATT.D: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB. Values greater than 40dB will typically produce a hard notch rather than a modest attenuation of motor noise.

INS_HNTC2_HMNCS.D: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of 0 disables this filter. The first harmonic refers to the base frequency.

INS_HNTC2_REF.D: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value

KDE_NPOLE.D: Sets the number of motor poles to calculate the correct RPM value

LAND_SPD_MS.D: The descent speed for the final stage of landing in m/s

LAND_SPD_HIGH_MS.D: The descent speed for the first stage of landing in m/s. If this is zero then WP_SPD_DN is used

LAND_ALT_LOW_M.D: Altitude during Landing at which vehicle slows to LAND_SPD_MS

LGR_DEPLOY_PIN.D: Pin number to use for detection of gear deployment. If set to -1 feedback is disabled. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

LGR_DEPLOY_POL.D: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when gear are deployed. If set to 0 then then deployed gear level is low.

LGR_WOW_PIN.D: Pin number to use for feedback of weight on wheels condition. If set to -1 feedback is disabled. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

LGR_WOW_POL.d: Weight on wheels feedback pin polarity
LGR_WOW_POL.D: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when there is weight on wheels. If set to 0 then then weight on wheels level is low.

LGR_DEPLOY_ALT.D: Altitude where the landing gear will be deployed. This should be lower than the RETRACT_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for deploying landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

LGR_RETRACT_ALT.D: Altitude where the landing gear will be retracted. This should be higher than the DEPLOY_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for retracting landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

LGR_OPTIONS.D: Options to retract or deploy landing gear in Auto or Guided mode

LOG_BACKEND_TYPE.D: Bitmap of what Logger backend types to enable. Block-based logging is available on SITL and boards with dataflash chips. Multiple backends can be selected.

LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE.d: Logging File and Block Backend buffer size max (in kibibytes)
LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE.D: The File and Block backends use a buffer to store data before writing to the block device. Raising this value may reduce "gaps" in your SD card logging but increases memory usage. This buffer size may be reduced to free

LOG_DISARMED.D: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled at all times including when disarmed. Logging before arming can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues and is necessary

LOG_REPLAY.d: Enable logging of information needed for Replay
LOG_REPLAY.D: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 and EKF3 state estimators will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. LOG_DISARMED must be set to 1 or 2 or else the log will not contain t

LOG_FILE_DSRMROT.d: Stop logging to current file on disarm
LOG_FILE_DSRMROT.D: When set, the current log file is closed when the vehicle is disarmed. If LOG_DISARMED is set then a fresh log will be opened. Applies to the File and Block logging backends.

LOG_MAV_BUFSIZE.d: Maximum AP_Logger MAVLink Backend buffer size
LOG_MAV_BUFSIZE.D: Maximum amount of memory to allocate to AP_Logger-over-mavlink

LOG_FILE_TIMEOUT.d: Timeout before giving up on file writes
LOG_FILE_TIMEOUT.D: This controls the amount of time before failing writes to a log file cause the file to be closed and logging stopped.

LOG_FILE_MB_FREE.d: Old logs on the SD card will be deleted to maintain this amount of free space
LOG_FILE_MB_FREE.D: Set this such that the free space is larger than your largest typical flight log

LOG_FILE_RATEMAX.d: Maximum logging rate for file backend
LOG_FILE_RATEMAX.D: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the file backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

LOG_MAV_RATEMAX.d: Maximum logging rate for mavlink backend
LOG_MAV_RATEMAX.D: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the mavlink backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

LOG_BLK_RATEMAX.d: Maximum logging rate for block backend
LOG_BLK_RATEMAX.D: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the block backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

LOG_DARM_RATEMAX.D: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to any backend when disarmed. A value of zero means that the normal backend rate limit is applied.

LOG_MAX_FILES.D: This sets the maximum number of log file that will be written on dataflash or sd card before starting to rotate log number. Limit is capped at 500 logs.

LOIT_ANG_MAX.D: Loiter maximum pilot requested lean angle. Set to zero for 2/3 of PSC_ANGLE_MAX/ATC_ANGLE_MAX. The maximum vehicle lean angle is still limited by PSC_ANGLE_MAX/ATC_ANGLE_MAX

LOIT_SPEED_MS.D: Defines the maximum speed in m/s which the aircraft will travel horizontally while in loiter mode

LOIT_ACC_MAX_M.D: Loiter maximum correction acceleration in m/s/s. Higher values cause the copter to correct position errors more aggressively.

LOIT_BRK_ACC_M.D: Loiter braking acceleration in m/s/s. Higher values stop the copter more quickly when the stick is centered.

LOIT_BRK_JRK_M.D: Loiter braking jerk in m/s/s/s. Higher values will remove braking faster if the pilot moves the sticks during a braking maneuver.

MIS_TOTAL.D: The number of mission mission items that has been loaded by the ground station. Do not change this manually.

MIS_RESTART.d: Mission Restart when entering Auto mode
MIS_RESTART.D: Controls mission starting point when entering Auto mode (either restart from beginning of mission or resume from last command run)

MIS_OPTIONS.D: Bitmask of what options to use in missions. If the DontZeroCounter counter option is set than on completion of a jump loop the counter is left at zero, so the jump will not happen again if the loop is re-entered.

MNT1_DEFLT_MODE.D: Mount default operating mode on startup and after control is returned from autopilot

MNT1_RC_RATE.D: Pilot rate control's maximum rate. Set to zero to use angle control

MNT1_RETRACT_X.d: Mount roll angle when in retracted position

MNT1_RETRACT_Y.d: Mount pitch angle when in retracted position

MNT1_RETRACT_Z.d: Mount yaw angle when in retracted position

MNT1_NEUTRAL_X.d: Mount roll angle when in neutral position

MNT1_NEUTRAL_Y.d: Mount pitch angle when in neutral position

MNT1_NEUTRAL_Z.d: Mount yaw angle when in neutral position

MNT1_LEAD_RLL.D: Servo mount roll angle output leads the vehicle angle by this amount of time based on current roll rate. Increase until the servo is responsive but does not overshoot

MNT1_LEAD_PTCH.D: Servo mount pitch angle output leads the vehicle angle by this amount of time based on current pitch rate. Increase until the servo is responsive but does not overshoot

MNT1_SYSID_DFLT.D: Default Target sysID for the mount to point to

MNT1_DEVID.D: Mount device ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

MNT1_OPTIONS.D: Mount options bitmask, note bit 2 only impacts RC targetting mode
v: bit0: RC lock state from previous mode
bit1: Return to neutral angles on RC failsafe
bit2: Force FPV (bf) lock on roll and pitch

MNT2_DEFLT_MODE.D: Mount default operating mode on startup and after control is returned from autopilot

MOT_THST_HOVER.D: Motor thrust needed to hover expressed as a number from 0 to 1

MOT_SLEW_DN_TIME.d: Output slew time for decreasing throttle

OA_MARGIN_MAX.D: Minimum distance in meters that the vehicle will try to stay away from obstacles and fences. BendyRuler only accepts a candidate path whose clearance exceeds this, and Dijkstra uses it as the margin held from fences. Thi

OA_OPTIONS.d: Options while recovering from Object Avoidance

OA_BR_LOOKAHEAD.d: Object Avoidance look ahead distance maximum
OA_BR_LOOKAHEAD.D: Object Avoidance will look this many meters ahead of vehicle

OA_BR_CONT_ANGLE.d: BendyRuler's bearing change resistance threshold angle
OA_BR_CONT_ANGLE.D: BendyRuler will resist changing current bearing if the change in bearing is over this angle

OA_DB_QUEUE_SIZE.D: OADatabase queue maximum number of points. This in an input buffer size. Larger means it can handle larger bursts of incoming data points to filter into the database. No impact on cpu, only RAM. Recommend larger for fast

PHLD_BRK_ANGLE.D: PosHold flight mode's max lean angle during braking in degrees

PLND_YAW_ALIGN.D: Yaw angle from body x-axis to sensor x-axis.

PLND_LAND_OFS_X.D: Desired landing position of the camera forward of the target in vehicle body frame

PLND_LAND_OFS_Y.D: desired landing position of the camera right of the target in vehicle body frame

PLND_EST_TYPE.D: Specifies the estimation method to be used

PLND_ACC_P_NSE.D: Kalman Filter Accelerometer Noise, higher values weight the input from the camera more, accels less

PLND_CAM_POS_X.D: X position of the camera in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin.

PLND_CAM_POS_Y.D: Y position of the camera in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin.

PLND_CAM_POS_Z.D: Z position of the camera in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin.

PLND_BUS.D: Precland sensor bus for I2C sensors.

PLND_LAG.D: Precision Landing sensor lag, to cope with variable landing_target latency

PLND_XY_DIST_MAX.d: Precision Landing maximum distance to target before descending
PLND_XY_DIST_MAX.D: The vehicle will not start descending if the landing target is detected and it is further than this many meters away. Set 0 to always descend.

PLND_STRICT.D: How strictly should the vehicle land on the target if target is lost

PLND_RET_MAX.d: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing
PLND_RET_MAX.D: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing. Set to zero to disable landing retry.

PLND_TIMEOUT.D: Time for which vehicle continues descend even if target is lost. After this time period, vehicle will attempt a landing retry depending on PLND_STRICT parameter.

PLND_RET_BEHAVE.D: Prec Land will do the action selected by this parameter if a retry to a landing is needed

PLND_ALT_MIN.D: Vehicle will continue landing vertically even if target is lost below this height. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zero to disable this.

PLND_ALT_MAX.D: Vehicle will continue landing vertically until this height if target is not found. Below this height if landing target is not found, landing retry/failsafe might be attempted. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zer

v: bit1: Allow Precision Landing after manual reposition
bit2: Maintain high speed in final descent

PSC_D_POS_P.D: Position (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between the desired altitude and actual altitude into a climb or descent rate which is passed to the throttle rate controller. Previously _POSZ_P.

PSC_NE_POS_P.D: Position controller P gain. Converts the distance (in the latitude direction) to the target location into a desired speed which is then passed to the loiter latitude rate controller. Previously _POSXY_P.

PSC_ANGLE_MAX.D: Maximum lean angle autopilot can request. Set to zero to use ANGLE_MAX parameter value

PSC_NE_JERK.d: Jerk limit for the horizontal kinematic input shaping
PSC_NE_JERK.D: Jerk limit of the horizontal kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

PSC_D_JERK.d: Jerk limit for the vertical kinematic input shaping
PSC_D_JERK.D: Jerk limit of the vertical kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

PSC_D_VEL_P.D: Velocity (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller. Previously _VELZ_P.

PSC_D_VEL_I.D: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELZ_I.

PSC_D_VEL_IMAX.D: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _VELZ_IMAX * 0.01.

PSC_D_VEL_D.D: Velocity (vertical) controller D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity. Previously _VELZ_D.

PSC_D_VEL_FF.D: Velocity (vertical) controller Feed Forward gain. Produces an output that is proportional to the magnitude of the target. Previously _VELZ_FF.

PSC_D_VEL_FLTE.D: Velocity (vertical) error filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms. Previously _VELZ_FLTE.

PSC_D_VEL_FLTD.d: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term
PSC_D_VEL_FLTD.D: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D terms. Previously _VELZ_FLTD.

PSC_D_ACC_P.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration into a motor output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

PSC_D_ACC_I.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_I * 0.1.

PSC_D_ACC_IMAX.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm that the I term will generate. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_IMAX * 0.001.

PSC_D_ACC_D.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired vertical acceleration vs actual acceleration. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_D * 0.1.

PSC_D_ACC_FF.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller feed forward. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_FF * 0.1.

PSC_D_ACC_FLTT.d: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz
PSC_D_ACC_FLTT.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTT.

PSC_D_ACC_FLTE.d: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz
PSC_D_ACC_FLTE.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTE.

PSC_D_ACC_FLTD.d: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz
PSC_D_ACC_FLTD.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTD.

PSC_D_ACC_SMAX.D: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. Thi

PSC_D_ACC_PDMX.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

PSC_D_ACC_D_FF.D: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

PSC_D_ACC_NTF.D: Accel (vertical) Target notch filter index, zero disables. If upgrading from 4.6 this is Previously _ACCZ_NTF.

PSC_D_ACC_NEF.D: Accel (vertical) Error notch filter index, zero disables. If upgrading from 4.6 this is Previously _ACCZ_NEF.

PSC_NE_VEL_P.D: Velocity (horizontal) P gain. Converts the difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_P.

PSC_NE_VEL_I.D: Velocity (horizontal) I gain. Corrects long-term difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_I.

PSC_NE_VEL_D.D: Velocity (horizontal) D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity. Previously _VELXY_D.

PSC_NE_VEL_IMAX.D: Velocity (horizontal) integrator maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _VELXY_IMAX * 0.01.

PSC_NE_VEL_FLTE.D: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms. Previously _VELXY_FLTE.

PSC_NE_VEL_FLTD.D: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D term. Previously _VELXY_FLTD.

PSC_NE_VEL_FF.D: Velocity (horizontal) feed forward gain. Converts the difference between desired velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_FF.

RALLY_TOTAL.D: Number of rally points currently loaded

RALLY_LIMIT_KM.D: Maximum distance to rally point. If the closest rally point is more than this number of kilometers from the current position and the home location is closer than any of the rally points from the current position then do

RALLY_INCL_HOME.D: Controls if Home is included as a Rally point (i.e. as a safe landing place) for RTL

RC_OVERRIDE_TIME.D: Timeout after which RC overrides will no longer be used, and RC input will resume, 0 will disable RC overrides, -1 will never timeout, and continue using overrides until they are disabled

v: bit2: Ignore Receiver Failsafe bit but allow other RC failsafes if setup
bit5: Arming check throttle for 0 input
bit6: Skip the arming check for neutral Roll/Pitch/Yaw sticks
bit8: Use passthrough for CRSF telemetry
bit9: Suppress CRSF mode/rate message for ELRS systems
bit11: Use Link Quality for RSSI with CRSF
bit12: Annotate CRSF flight mode with * on disarm
bit14: Clear MAVLink overrides on any stick input

RC_PROTOCOLS.D: Bitmask of enabled RC protocols. Allows narrowing the protocol detection to only specific types of RC receivers which can avoid issues with incorrect detection. Set to 1 to enable all protocols.

RC_FS_TIMEOUT.D: RC failsafe will trigger this many seconds after loss of RC

RPM4_PIN.D: Which digital GPIO pin to use. Only used on type = GPIO. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

RPM4_ESC_MASK.d: Bitmask of ESC telemetry channels to average
RPM4_ESC_MASK.D: Mask of channels which support ESC rpm telemetry. RPM telemetry of the selected channels will be averaged

RPM4_ESC_INDEX.d: ESC Telemetry Index to write RPM to
RPM4_ESC_INDEX.D: ESC Telemetry Index to write RPM to. Use 0 to disable.

RPM4_DC_ID.D: DroneCAN sensor ID to assign to this backend

RSSI_TYPE.D: Radio Receiver RSSI type. If your radio receiver supports RSSI of some kind, set it here, then set its associated RSSI_XXXXX parameters, if any.

RSSI_ANA_PIN.D: Pin used to read the RSSI voltage or PWM value. Analog Airspeed ports can be used for Analog inputs (some autopilots provide others also), Non-IOMCU Servo/MotorOutputs can be used for PWM input when configured as "GPIOs"

RSSI_PIN_LOW.D: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_PIN_HIGH. When using pin 103, the maximum value

RSSI_PIN_HIGH.D: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_PIN_LOW. When using pin 103, the maximum value

RSSI_CHANNEL.D: The channel number where RSSI will be output by the radio receiver (5 and above).

RSSI_CHAN_LOW.D: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_CHAN_HIGH

RSSI_CHAN_HIGH.D: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_CHAN_LOW

RTL_ALT_M.D: The minimum alt above home the vehicle will climb to before returning. If the vehicle is flying higher than this value it will return at its current altitude.

RTL_ALT_FINAL_M.D: Altitude the vehicle will move to as the final stage of Returning to Launch or after completing a mission. Set to zero to land.

RTL_CLIMB_MIN_M.D: The vehicle will climb this many meters during the initial climb portion of the RTL

RTL_SPEED_MS.D: The speed in m/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain horizontally while flying home. If this is set to zero, WP_SPD will be used instead.

SCHED_DEBUG.D: Set to non-zero to enable scheduler debug messages. When set to show "Slips" the scheduler will display a message whenever a scheduled task is delayed due to too much CPU load. When set to ShowOverruns the scheduled will

SCHED_LOOP_RATE.D: This controls the rate of the main control loop in Hz. This should only be changed by developers. This only takes effect on restart. Values over 400 are considered highly experimental.

SCHED_OPTIONS.D: This controls optional aspects of the scheduler.

SCR_VM_I_COUNT.D: The number virtual machine instructions that can be run before considering a script to have taken an excessive amount of time

SCR_HEAP_SIZE.D: Amount of memory available for scripting

v: bit0: No Scripts to run message if all scripts have stopped
bit1: Runtime messages for memory usage and execution time
bit2: Suppress logging scripts to dataflash
bit3: log runtime memory usage and execution time

SIM_SLUP_SYSID.D: Slung Payload MAVLink system id to distinguish it from others on the same network

SIM_SONAR_GLITCH.D: Probablility a sonar glitch would happen

SIM_SONAR_OFFSET.D: Sonar measurement offset, in meters. Can be used for error injection.

SIM_SONAR_POS_X.D: XYZ position of the sonar relative to the body frame origin (X-axis)

SIM_SONAR_POS_Y.D: XYZ position of the sonar relative to the body frame origin (Y-axis)

SIM_SONAR_POS_Z.D: XYZ position of the sonar relative to the body frame origin (Z-axis)

SIM_SONAR_RND.D: Scaling factor for simulated sonar noise

SIM_SONAR_SCALE.D: Sonar conversion scale from distance to voltage

SIM_SPEEDUP.D: Runs the simulation at multiples of normal speed. Do not use if realtime physics, like RealFlight, is being used

SIM_SPR_ENABLE.D: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the Sprayer simulation

SIM_SPR_PUMP.D: The pin number that the Sprayer pump is connected to. (start at 1)

SIM_SPR_SPIN.D: The pin number that the Sprayer spinner servo is connected to. (start at 1)

SIM_TA_ENABLE.D: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the simulated tonealarm

SIM_TEMP_BFACTOR.D: A pressure change with temperature that closely matches what has been observed with a ICM-20789

SIM_TEMP_BRD_OFF.D: Barometer board temperature offset from atmospheric temperature

SIM_TETH_DENSITY.D: Linear mass density of the tether wire

SIM_TETH_DMPCNST.D: Damping constant for the tether to simulate resistance based on change in stretch

SIM_TETH_ENABLE.D: Enable or disable the tether simulation

SIM_TETH_LINELEN.D: Maximum length of the tether line in meters

SIM_TETH_SPGCNST.D: Spring constant for the tether to simulate elastic forces when stretched beyond its maximum length

SIM_TETH_STUCK.D: Enable or disable a stuck tether simulation

SIM_TETH_SYSID.D: MAVLink system ID for the tether simulation, used to distinguish it from other systems on the network

SIM_THML_SCENARI.D: Scenario for thermalling simulation, for soaring

SIM_TIDE_DIR.D: Tide direction wave is coming from

SIM_TIME_JITTER.D: Upper limit of random jitter in loop time

SIM_TWIST_TIME.D: Time that twist is applied on the vehicle

SIM_TWIST_X.D: Rotational acceleration of twist x axis

SIM_TWIST_Y.D: Rotational acceleration of twist y axis

SIM_TWIST_Z.D: Rotational acceleration of twist z axis

SIM_UART_LOSS.D: Sets percentage of outgoing byte loss on UARTs

SIM_VIB_FREQ_X.D: Frequency of vibration applied to IMU readings in SITL (X-axis)

SIM_VIB_FREQ_Y.D: Frequency of vibration applied to IMU readings in SITL (Y-axis)

SIM_VIB_FREQ_Z.D: Frequency of vibration applied to IMU readings in SITL (Z-axis)

SIM_VIB_MOT_MASK.D: Motor mask, allowing external simulators to mark motors

SIM_VIB_MOT_MAX.D: Max frequency to use as baseline for adding motor noise for the gyros and accels

SIM_VIB_MOT_MULT.D: Amplitude scaling of motor noise relative to gyro/accel noise

SIM_VICON_POS_X.d: SITL vicon position on vehicle in Forward direction

SIM_VICON_POS_Y.d: SITL vicon position on vehicle in Right direction

SIM_VICON_POS_Z.d: SITL vicon position on vehicle in Down direction

SIM_VICON_P_SD.d: SITL vicon position standard deviation for gaussian noise

SIM_VICON_QUAL.D: SITL vicon odometry quality field sent in MAVLink ODOMETRY message (-1=failure, 0=unknown, 1-100=quality)

SIM_VICON_V_SD.d: SITL vicon velocity standard deviation for gaussian noise

SIM_VICON_YAW.d: SITL vicon yaw angle in earth frame

SIM_VICON_YAWERR.D: SITL vicon yaw added to reported yaw sent to vehicle

SIM_VOLZ_ENA.D: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the Volz simulator

SIM_VOLZ_FMASK.D: fail servo at current position. Channel 1 is bit 0.

SIM_VOLZ_MASK.D: mask of servo output channels to override with values from Volz protocol. Note these are indexed from 0 - so channel 3 (usually throttle) has value 4 in this bitmask (1<<2).

SIM_WIND_DIR.d: Direction simulated wind is coming from
SIM_WIND_DIR.D: Allows you to set wind direction (true deg) in sim

SIM_WIND_DIR_Z.D: Allows you to set vertical wind direction (true deg) in sim. 0 means pure horizontal wind. 90 means pure updraft.

SIM_WIND_SPD.D: Allows you to emulate wind in sim

SIM_WIND_T.D: Selects how wind varies from surface to WIND_T_ALT

SIM_WIND_TC.D: this controls the time over which wind changes take effect

SIM_WIND_TURB.D: Allows you to emulate random wind variations in sim

SIM_WIND_T_ALT.D: Altitude at which wind reaches full strength, decaying from full strength as altitude lowers to ground level

SIM_WIND_T_COEF.D: For linear wind profile,wind is reduced by (Altitude-WIND_T_ALT) x this value

SIM_WOW_PIN.D: SITL set this simulated pin to true if vehicle is on ground

SPRAY_ENABLE.D: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the sprayer

SPRAY_PUMP_RATE.D: Desired pump speed when travelling 1m/s expressed as a percentage

SPRAY_SPINNER.D: Spinner's rotation speed in PWM (a higher rate will disperse the spray over a wider area horizontally)

SPRAY_SPEED_MIN.D: Speed minimum at which we will begin spraying

SPRAY_PUMP_MIN.D: Minimum pump speed expressed as a percentage

SRTL_ACCURACY.D: SmartRTL accuracy. The minimum distance between points.

SRTL_POINTS.d: SmartRTL maximum number of points on path
SRTL_POINTS.D: SmartRTL maximum number of points on path. Set to 0 to disable SmartRTL. 100 points consumes about 3k of memory.

STAT_BOOTCNT.D: Number of times board has been booted

STAT_RESET.D: Seconds since January 1st 2016 (Unix epoch+1451606400) since statistics reset (set to 0 to reset statistics, other set values will be ignored)

STAT_DISTFLWN.D: Estimate of total distance flown since statistics reset

TCAL_ENABLED.D: Enable temperature calibration. Set to 0 to disable. Set to 1 to use learned values. Set to 2 to learn new values and use the values

TCAL_TEMP_MIN.D: Minimum learned temperature. This is automatically set by the learning process

TCAL_TEMP_MAX.D: Maximum learned temperature. This is automatically set by the learning process

TCAL_BARO_EXP.D: Learned exponent for barometer temperature correction

TMODE_ENABLE.D: tmode (or "toy" mode) gives a simplified user interface designed for mass market drones. Version1 is for the SkyViper V2450GPS. Version2 is for the F412 based boards

TMODE_MODE1.D: This is the initial mode when the vehicle is first turned on. This mode is assumed to not require GPS

TMODE_MODE2.D: This is the secondary mode. This mode is assumed to require GPS

Q_P_D_ACC_FLTD.D: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTD.

Q_P_NE_VEL_FF.D: Velocity (horizontal) feed forward gain. Converts the difference between desired velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_FF.

Q_TAILSIT_VT_P_P.D: Scale from PID output to control surface, for use where a single axis is actuated by both motors and Tilt/control surface on a copter style tailsitter, increase to favor control surfaces and reduce motor output by reduci

Q_TILT_WING_FLAP.d: Tiltrotor tilt angle that will be used as flap

Q_WP_RFND_USE.D: This controls if waypoint missions use rangefinder for terrain following

Q_WP_JERK.D: Defines the horizontal jerk in m/s/s used during missions

RLL_RATE_D_FF.D: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

RLL_RATE_NTF.D: Roll Target notch filter index, zero disables

RLL_RATE_NEF.D: Roll Error notch filter index, zero disables

RLL2SRV_ACCEL.D: Roll acceleration limit. Setting to zero disables input shaping.

SOAR_ENABLE.D: Toggles the soaring mode on and off

SOAR_Q2.D: Standard deviation of noise in process for position and radius

SOAR_MIN_THML_S.D: Minimum number of seconds to spend thermalling

SOAR_MIN_CRSE_S.D: Minimum number of seconds to spend cruising

SOAR_ALT_MAX.D: Don't thermal any higher than this.

SOAR_ALT_CUTOFF.d: Maximum power altitude, relative to the home location
SOAR_ALT_CUTOFF.D: Cut off throttle at this alt.

SOAR_THML_ARSPD.D: If non-zero this airspeed will be used when thermalling. A value of 0 will use AIRSPEED_CRUISE.

STEER2SRV_P.D: The proportional gain for steering. This should be approximately equal to the diameter of the turning circle of the vehicle at low speed and maximum steering angle

STEER2SRV_I.D: This is the gain from the integral of steering angle. Increasing this gain causes the controller to trim out steady offsets due to an out of trim vehicle.

STEER2SRV_D.D: This adjusts the damping of the steering control loop. This gain helps to reduce steering jitter with vibration. It should be increased in 0.01 increments as too high a value can lead to a high frequency steering oscilla

STEER2SRV_IMAX.D: This limits the number of degrees of steering in centi-degrees over which the integrator will operate. At the default setting of 1500 centi-degrees, the integrator will be limited to +- 15 degrees of servo travel. The ma

STEER2SRV_MINSPD.D: This is the minimum assumed ground speed in meters/second for steering. Having a minimum speed prevents oscillations when the vehicle first starts moving. The vehicle can still drive slower than this limit, but the steer

STEER2SRV_FF.D: The feed forward gain for steering this is the ratio of the achieved turn rate to applied steering. A value of 1 means that the vehicle would yaw at a rate of 45 degrees per second with full steering deflection at 1m/s g

STEER2SRV_DRTSPD.D: Speed after that the maximum degree of steering will start to derate. Set this speed to a maximum speed that a plane can do controlled turn at maximum angle of steering wheel without rolling to wing. If 0 then no deratin

STEER2SRV_DRTMIN.D: The angle that limits smallest angle of steering wheel at maximum speed. Even if it should derate below, it will stop derating at this angle.

TECS_SINK_MIN.D: Minimum sink rate when at THR_MIN and AIRSPEED_CRUISE.

TECS_TIME_CONST.D: Time constant of the TECS control algorithm. Small values make faster altitude corrections but can cause overshoot and aggressive behavior.

TECS_THR_DAMP.D: Damping gain for throttle demand loop. Increase to add throttle activity to dampen oscillations in speed and height.

TECS_INTEG_GAIN.D: Integrator gain to trim out long-term speed and height errors.

TECS_VERT_ACC.D: Maximum vertical acceleration used to correct speed or height errors.

TECS_HGT_OMEGA.D: This is the cross-over frequency of the complementary filter used to fuse vertical acceleration and baro alt to obtain an estimate of height rate and height.

TECS_SPD_OMEGA.D: This is the cross-over frequency of the complementary filter used to fuse longitudinal acceleration and airspeed to obtain a lower noise and lag estimate of airspeed.

TECS_RLL2THR.D: Gain from bank angle to throttle to compensate for loss of airspeed from drag in turns. Set to approximately 10x the sink rate in m/s caused by a 45-degree turn. High efficiency models may need less while less efficient

TECS_PTCH_DAMP.D: Damping gain for pitch control from TECS control. Increasing may correct for oscillations in speed and height, but too much may cause additional oscillation and degraded control.

TECS_SINK_MAX.D: Maximum demanded descent rate. Do not set higher than the vertical speed the aircraft can maintain at THR_MIN, TECS_PITCH_MIN, and AIRSPEED_MAX.

TECS_LAND_ARSPD.D: When performing an autonomous landing, this value is used as the goal airspeed during approach. Max airspeed allowed is Trim Airspeed or AIRSPEED_MAX as defined by LAND_OPTIONS bitmask. Note that this parameter is not us

TECS_LAND_THR.D: Use this parameter instead of LAND_ARSPD if your platform does not have an airspeed sensor. It is the cruise throttle during landing approach. If this value is negative then it is disabled and TECS_LAND_ARSPD is used ins

TECS_LAND_SINK.d: Sink rate for final landing stage
TECS_LAND_SINK.D: The sink rate in meters/second for the final stage of landing.

TECS_LAND_DAMP.D: This is the sink rate gain for the pitch demand loop when in final landing stage of flight. It should be larger than TECS_PTCH_DAMP to allow for better sink rate control during flare.

TECS_LAND_PMAX.d: Maximum pitch during final stage of landing
TECS_LAND_PMAX.D: This limits the pitch used during the final stage of automatic landing. During the final landing stage most planes need to keep their pitch small to avoid stalling. A maximum of 10 degrees is usually good. A value of zer

TECS_APPR_SMAX.D: The sink rate max for the landing approach stage of landing. This will need to be large for steep landing approaches especially when using reverse thrust. If 0, then use TECS_SINK_MAX.

TECS_LAND_SRC.D: When zero, the flare sink rate (TECS_LAND_SINK) is a fixed sink demand. With this enabled the flare sink rate will increase/decrease the flare sink demand as you get further beyond the LAND waypoint. Has no effect before

TECS_LAND_PDAMP.D: This is the damping gain for the pitch demand loop during landing. Increase to add damping to correct for oscillations in speed and height. If set to 0 then TECS_PTCH_DAMP will be used instead.

TECS_SYNAIRSPEED.D: This enables the use of synthetic airspeed in TECS for aircraft that don't have a real airspeed sensor. This is useful for development testing where the user is aware of the considerable limitations of the synthetic airs

TECS_OPTIONS.D: This allows the enabling of special features in the speed/height controller.

TECS_PTCH_FF_K.D: This parameter sets the gain between demanded airspeed and pitch. It has units of radians per metre per second and should generally be negative. A good starting value is -0.04 for gliders and -0.08 for draggy airframes.

TUNE_PARAM.D: This sets which parameter or set of parameters will be tuned. Values greater than 100 indicate a set of parameters rather than a single parameter. Parameters less than 50 are for QuadPlane vertical lift motors only.

TUNE_CHAN_MIN.D: This sets the PWM lower limit for the tuning channel

TUNE_CHAN_MAX.D: This sets the PWM upper limit for the tuning channel

TUNE_MODE_REVERT.D: This controls whether tuning values will revert on a flight mode change.

TUNE_ERR_THRESH.D: This sets the controller error threshold above which an alarm will sound and a message will be sent to the GCS to warn of controller instability while tuning. The error is the rms value of the P+D corrections in the loop
